title: Mirabel and the Veil
premise: Jonah Fairweather, an exiled storm-caller hiding as a charm-seller in the magic-free city of Greyhollow, learns that King Aldric has declared a hunt for the gifted—because something ancient wearing the king's face is consuming his memories and turning his fear into law. Jonah is dragged back into a world he fled when a runaway girl named Mirabel arrives bearing his sister's storm-mark and a fragment of the king's stolen memories. To end the hunt and save both the girl and the crown, Jonah must breach the Veil between the living world and the memory-realm where the usurper nests, unbinding Aldric before the long winter finishes falling. He succeeds at terrible cost: he gives up his own storm to seal the Veil, but finds a new family—and a quieter kind of magic—in what remains.
about_author: Isandro Lockridge is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing letters from families separated by border wars, an experience that haunts every found-family story they tell. They write fantasy about inheritance—the things we're given, the things we refuse, and the memories we choose to keep.

chapters.title: The Charm Seller's Winter
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. In Greyhollow, Jonah sells luck-knots and fever-charms that are deliberately useless, keeping his storm-calling buried for twelve years. A routine inspection by the Ministry of Order leaves him shaken but safe. Emotional beat: the exhausting vigilance of a life built on being small.

chapters.title: A Proclamation in Ash
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Criers announce the king's Edict of Cleansing: all gifted persons must register or be hunted. Jonah's neighbor Tam, a hedge-healer, is taken that night. Jonah burns his mother's grimoire page by page. Emotional beat: grief disguised as pragmatism; the illusion of safety dies.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Fell Through
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. A feral eleven-year-old with a storm-mark on her wrist crashes through Jonah's window during a curfew sweep, pursued by hunters. She carries a locket humming with someone else's memories. Emotional beat: reluctant rescue; Jonah recognizes his sister's mark and cannot turn her away.

chapters.title: What the Locket Remembers
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The locket holds fragments of King Aldric's true memories—a gentle man, a dead queen, a bargain made at the Veil. Mirabel doesn't know how she got it. Jonah realizes the 'king' hunting magicians isn't the king at all. Emotional beat: dread crystallizing into purpose.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV, with flashback. Why Jonah was exiled: his storm killed his village's harvest-guard, including his sister Wren—or so he believed. The mark on Mirabel suggests Wren survived and sent the girl. Emotional beat: guilt confronted; the past refuses to stay buried.

chapters.title: The Undertow Beneath Greyhollow
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Mirabel leads Jonah through smuggler tunnels to the Undertow, a hidden community of unregistered gifted folk led by the one-eyed ferrywoman Sable Voss. Emotional beat: first glimpse of found family; hope that feels dangerous to accept.

chapters.title: Sable's Bargain
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Sable agrees to hide Mirabel if Jonah uses his storm to open the old sea-gate before winter ice seals the harbor—the community's only supply route. Jonah hasn't called weather in twelve years. Emotional beat: terror of his own power versus responsibility to others.

chapters.title: First Thunder
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. At the sea-gate, Jonah calls a small storm; it answers too eagerly, nearly drowning the smugglers. Mirabel's presence steadies him—her mark harmonizes with his. Emotional beat: power as relationship, not weapon; fragile trust forming.

chapters.title: Hunters at the Door
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The king's hunters, led by the memory-eaten Captain Ives, raid the Undertow. Sable covers their escape and is captured. Mirabel blames herself. Emotional beat: survivor's guilt; the cost of belonging.

chapters.title: The Court of Hollow Men
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Disguised as a clerk, Jonah infiltrates the palace and sees the thing wearing Aldric's crown: the Regent of Rust, a memory-devourer feeding on the king while the real Aldric wastes in a locked tower, forgetting his own name. Emotional beat: horror tempered by pity for the hollowed king.

chapters.title: A King Who Forgets His Name
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. In the tower, Aldric clings to three memories: his queen's laugh, his daughter's lullaby, and a promise he made at the Veil. He scratches them into the wall each day as they fade. Emotional beat: dignity inside dissolution; what makes a self.

chapters.title: Wren's Mark
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The locket reveals its origin: Wren Fairweather lives, exiled to the memory-realm beyond the Veil after the accident, sending Mirabel out as her hand and voice. Mirabel must tell Jonah. Emotional beat: joy and fury entangled; the sister he mourned is alive and unreachable.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Begins
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The Regent accelerates the hunt; snow falls black with ash-magic, and the Veil thins across the city. Ives, half-consumed, warns Jonah that the Regent intends to devour every gifted mind to complete its embodiment. Emotional beat: the clock starts ticking; no more hiding.

chapters.title: What We Bury, What We Keep
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. In the Undertow's refuge, survivors share memories freely so none can be stolen whole—Mirabel learns found family means letting others carry your past. She gives Jonah her memory of Wren's message: 'Come to the Veil. Bring the storm home.' Emotional beat: grief transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Storm-Called
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah fully reclaims his gift in a night of training with Mirabel, learning that his exile was engineered—the Regent fed his storm the harvest-guard's death to break him. Emotional beat: rage, then release; the villain authored his shame.

chapters.title: The Rescue of Captain Ives
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Mirabel and Jonah free Sable and the captured Undertow folk from the palace dungeons, and Mirabel restores a sliver of Ives's memories via the locket, turning him. Emotional beat: mercy as strategy and grace; even broken people can choose again.

chapters.title: The Tower Wall
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah reaches Aldric and reads the scratched memories aloud nightly, anchoring the king's self against the Regent's pull. Aldric, lucid for one hour, tells Jonah how the Veil can be opened—and what it will cost. Emotional beat: two broken men trading honesty in the dark.

chapters.title: Crossing the Veil
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. During the solstice eclipse, Jonah, Mirabel, and Ives cross into the memory-realm: a frozen landscape of everything the Regent has eaten. They find Wren, aged barely a day per year, guarding a door of storms. Emotional beat: reunion suspended in awe and heartbreak.

chapters.title: The Thing That Wears the Crown
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Confrontation with the Regent at the heart of the memory-realm, which offers Jonah his erased memories and Wren's freedom in exchange for the city's gifted minds. Wren reveals she stayed willingly, caging the Regent's hunger—her sacrifice, not her punishment. Emotional beat: temptation met with love.

chapters.title: Unbinding the King
chapters.summary: Climax. Jonah pours his entire storm into the binding that anchors Aldric, while Mirabel and Wren sing the lullaby-memory that gives the Regent's stolen selves somewhere to return. The Regent unravels; Aldric wakes whole; the Veil begins to close—but only from the far side. Emotional beat: sacrifice chosen freely, family holding the line together.

chapters.title: The Quiet After Snow
chapters.summary: Falling action. Wren stays behind to hold the Veil shut; Jonah gives up his storm forever, becoming simply a man. Aldric repeals the Edict publicly, naming the gifted protectors of the realm. Jonah grieves his sister a second time, differently. Emotional beat: loss braided with peace.

chapters.title: Mirabel and the Veil
chapters.summary: Resolution, Mirabel's POV. One year later: Jonah runs a school for gifted children in Greyhollow, Mirabel his first student and adopted daughter. Each solstice they visit the sea-gate, where the wind carries a familiar hum—Wren, listening. Emotional beat: inheritance transformed; family is what we build and keep.
